Depending on the input string, transforming it to all uppercase letters might lead to unexpected results. The code should correctly handle scenarios based on more refined conditions or specific character positions.

fix_code:
s = input()
count = 0
for c in s:
    if c.isupper():
        count += 1
# Refine the condition before transformation
# Transform to uppercase if majority of characters are uppercase
if count > len(s) / 2:  # More than half are uppercase
    s = s.upper()
else:
    s = s.lower()
print(s)
